title: All MCP tools declare an empty inputSchema — args undiscoverable by a real client
evidence: src/server.ts:14 builds every tool with inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: {}, additionalProperties: true } — no season/team/competition/etc. declared. tools/list therefore advertises zero params, yet handlers require them: standings/team_record/head_to_head/ask_question throw via required(args.X,'X') (server.ts:25-30, 35). The factual probe built args from the (empty) schema, sent {}, and recorded _factual.json note: 'no tool returned a 2019 Série A table naming Flamengo (tried 4 candidate tools)' → factual_accuracy=0.0. Server + 7 tools exist and dispatch correctly when args are supplied (store.test.ts tools/call passes {team,season} and gets 3 rows), so the server is present but not usably invocable by a discovering client.
suggestion: Populate each tool's inputSchema.properties with the actual parameters (season:number, team:string, competition:enum, ...) and mark required ones, so an MCP client can discover and pass them.

title: standings() double-counts overlapping seasons and splits one team into two rows
evidence: src/store.ts:77 standings() calls add(m.homeTeam,...) keying on the RAW team name (no normalise()), and findMatches (store.ts:41-49) filters only competition==='Brasileirão' + season with NO cross-source dedup. load() (store.ts:30-36) tags BOTH Brasileirao_Matches.csv (source 'serie-a') and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (source 'historic') as competition 'Brasileirão'. Verified: both files carry 380 rows each for seasons 2015-2019 (awk on the season/Ano columns). serie-a stores 'Flamengo-RJ' (state suffix), historic stores 'Flamengo' — so for 2015-2019 every fixture is counted twice AND Flamengo splits into two table rows. store.test.ts itself asserts standings(2023)[0].team==='Flamengo-RJ' (raw name kept). 2023 has only serie-a data so no split shows there, but the overlap seasons produce a structurally wrong table. This root cause also doubles team_record() and competition_statistics() (R6/R10) for Brasileirão 2015-2019.
suggestion: Deduplicate the two Brasileirão sources (prefer one per season, or key by normalised (date, teams)) and aggregate standings on normalise(team) instead of the raw name.

title: No cross-file dedup — Brasileirão aggregate stats double-count for 2015-2019
evidence: src/store.ts:18-38 load() concatenates all match files with no dedup; statistics() (store.ts:81-85) and record() (store.ts:57-66) reuse findMatches() over competition==='Brasileirão', which spans both serie-a and historic sources. For 2015-2019 (380 rows in each of Brasileirao_Matches.csv and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv) match counts, totalGoals, home/away/draw tallies and biggestWins all roughly double (average goals/match survives since numerator and denominator both double). The aggregate-stats capability itself is present and correct for non-overlapping seasons and non-Brasileirão competitions — scored implemented, but the double-count is a real data-integrity defect sharing R9's root cause.
suggestion: Add source dedup at load time so any season present in two files is not counted twice by statistics()/record().

title: 5 tests, 0 skipped — build+test gate passes
evidence: test/store.test.ts has 5 node:test cases, 0 .skip/xit/it.todo; scores.json test_coverage=1.0, defect_rate=1.0 → build succeeded and all tests passed.
suggestion: Add a test covering an overlapping season (e.g. standings(2019)) — it would immediately surface the double-count/split bug.
